rows.check: bundle aee466c15635: the source climate is read (129 grid, 12 snow months, moisture, rainfall; seed 73)
the fields have SandBox.MapScene's layouts (512^2 (x, y) floats, 32^2 (snow, rain) bytes) and the snow texture is 512^2 RGBA
the synthesis is deterministic; its identity covers the source, the seed, the coordinate layout, the policy and every field (the snow texture too)
every strip sample is an exact copy of its canonical sample (wind, snow/rain and the snow texture): the seam has no discontinuity
beyond the pole lines every column has one value (wind calm; the pole node's snow and rain): the pole is one location
the wind field is smooth (largest neighbour step 0.379498, at a band edge; below the official War Sails flowmap's mean step, 0.39) and bounded by the policy scale

the snow-season bytes are the inverse of the installed formula: 196 is Snowy all year, 155 for 9 months, 113 for 6, 72 for 3, 30 only at the peak, each the smallest such byte; the ice cap (255) all year

every weather node's Snowy share of the year equals its FWGC++ snow-season length (114 seasonal nodes, 788 ice-cap nodes Snowy all year; worst share error 0.0058 of a year): the snow byte is the inverse installed formula
the world has snowy and rainy weather nodes (902 and 1020 of 1024)
a weather node's rain recomputes from the source (8 x 8 footprint mean of rainfall over the layer maximum)
snow texture pixels recompute from the source (R the snow byte, G rain, B 0, A 255; row 0 at physical y = extent): 414 pixels
the texture's rows run against physical y (the north pole line at row 319, the south at row 191) and it is named by its hash (mnbl_snow_487982f9fd189506)
the scene's terrain names the world's snow texture once (dynamic_flowmap_texture_name), never a vanilla one; the name reads back
the permanent-white route names no texture (the scene names none), keeps the gameplay bytes and is a different climate identity
the in-memory binding answers with the engine's index (row * dim + col, col = floor(x / extent * dim)) for wind, snow/rain and colour grade, and carries the snow texture
the colour-grade grid has MapColorGradeManager's layout (512^2 bytes), only installed grade values, and is deterministic
the world shows several climate grades (20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120, 140)
colour-grade strip cells copy their canonical cells and the rows beyond each pole line carry one grade
colour-grade cells recompute from the source (nearest cell's biome, grassland split by moisture, water and other ids by temperature band, 3 x 3 mode filter): 111 cells, 6 changed by the filter
without the perturbation a mid-band sample is its band's direction at the policy scale, the north component mirrored in the southern hemisphere (map vector (east, -north); 52 samples)
the wind varies by latitude: neighbouring bands blow east and west in turn in both hemispheres, not one east-west wind (RT-18)
the perturbation is the world's (seed 73 repeats, seed 74 differs) and turns the wind within +-0.35 rad (-0.227799 to 0.30766)
a layout whose width is not a whole number of samples of every grid is refused (strip samples could not copy canonical ones)
a storm past a pole line is reflected back across it (one between the lines stays)
the storm spawn chance is scaled by the area of a weather node against Calradia's (1 at Calradia's spacing; 2.3669 here)
storms are born only at canonical positions between the pole lines (never in a strip or beyond a pole; anywhere on a world that is not periodic)
a position across the seam from a storm is measured at its copy beside the storm (5 units away, not width - 5)
a storm that leaves the canonical range is moved back by one width (none while canonical)
the MMR-63 fixture layout synthesizes its own fields from the same source (a different identity)
worldgen/policies/climate-flow.json names the code's version and constants
the policy reader refuses a snow-season byte the inverse rule does not give, an unknown snow route and another version
the bundle's water classes are read (ocean, lake, river, land)
the water body lies on the projection's datum (z = 0) and covers the whole terrain
the water body uses the installed War Sails water material, its water-body tag and the plane physics (as the MMR-59/63 fixtures)
a generated scene carries one water body and one colour-grade manager (a second manager is refused)
every lake body's level comes from the source's lake cells (159 bodies shown, 0 too shallow to clear their beds, 6816 lake samples)
every lake plane lies inside the terrain (the scene's box is the campaign map's borders)
each lake's plane clears its bed, never rises above another sample within one sample of its box, and is its source level projected as the terrain (level x 0.005) unless that would
every strip lake is a copy of a canonical lake one width away, at the same level, a copy cut by the terrain's edge at its whole twin's (80 strip copies, 2 cut by the edge)
a generated scene carries the sea plane and one plane per lake body, each a War Sails water body

stormPolicy.poleRule: a storm past a pole line is reflected back across it, its trail too, and its move direction turned towards the equator
stormPolicy.seamRule: a storm leaving the canonical range is moved by whole widths with its trail; effects use the party's copy nearest the storm
stormPolicy.spawnRule: open-sea weather nodes in the canonical range between the pole lines
